precedents.ruling: [assumed] From Farpoint on, the chief engineer is Lt. Cmdr. Sarah MacDougal, who came aboard at Deneb IV. Jim Shimoda is assistant chief engineer. Lt. Cmdr. Argyle is aboard as a senior engineer who holds the chief's watch on other shifts; the billet can change hands, as canon's season one shows.
precedents.reason: law.md leaves the chief engineer to the build. Canon shows MacDougal in the billet first after Farpoint (41209.2), with Shimoda as her assistant, and Argyle called one of the chief engineers soon after (card K-037).

precedents.ruling: [assumed] The saucer and stardrive are held by twelve docking clamps ('docking latches' in engineering usage); engineering monitors whether each is seated. After any separation a structural survey of the latches and the interface is standard; after an emergency separation at warp past the red line and a manual dock, real stress is plausible and the survey costs engineering time. The interface can be reached by a ventral crawlway from inside the ship.
precedents.reason: Canon shows clamps locking the joint and calls separation at warp a no-margin manoeuvre (K-038). Tidal shear at a field wall is already a failure mode of M-001; mechanism card M-017.

precedents.ruling: A parthenogenetic cardiac implant is fitted at a starbase or a well-equipped medical centre. The Enterprise's sickbay can stabilise a patient and, with notice, perform the surgery; a remote colony infirmary can only stabilise and evacuate. Sickbay has an intensive-care ward of a few biobeds plus ward space and private rooms; a mass-casualty load overflows into other spaces and takes staff from other duties.
precedents.reason: Picard's 2327 case shows distance from a facility can be fatal; his 2365 choice of a starbase shows where the surgery is ordinarily done (K-043). No on-screen bed count.

precedents.ruling: A defined-molecule or subunit vaccine, or a non-infectious inactivated preparation, can be replicated in quantity once its pattern is validated; each new product is tested for stability first, since some fail as the Ligonian vaccine did. Infectious agents, live attenuated strains included, are not replicated: they are grown in culture in the medical or biology labs, which takes time, space and staff.
precedents.reason: M-005 works at molecular resolution and canon bars living things; Code of Honor shows stability is checked product by product (K-044).

precedents.ruling: [assumed] Crew drills are the first officer's to schedule. Anything that takes the ship off her course or schedule, or separates her, needs the captain's approval.
precedents.reason: The first officer runs the ship day to day (law.md, Starfleet); the captain decides what changes her course.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] A Federation colony governs itself. In a declared outbreak, the attending Starfleet chief medical officer may impose a medical quarantine on people and traffic, which the colony may protest to the Federation but must obey. Killing a colony's animals or destroying habitat needs the colony's own authority, or the Federation Council's.
precedents.reason: Canon shows Starfleet medical officers declaring quarantines (Unnatural Selection) and colonies governing themselves; destroying property is not a medical power.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] A colony's charter on a world with native life binds it to preserve native ecosystems outside the zones it was allotted. Destroying habitat beyond them breaches the charter and is the Colonial Office's to judge, after the fact.
precedents.reason: Consistent with the Federation's caution about native life (Home Soil's terraforming ethics) without importing that episode's situation.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] Internal sensors can be set to flag, in a given space, any life sign that matches no crew record or authorised visitor, and the computer can raise an alert from sensors on its own (as it raised a collision alert at the Farpoint barrier). A standing automatic intruder alert is a security procedure; because it can set the ship's alert condition, it needs the captain's signature. Whether such a filter registers a canon unknown like Q is not known to anyone aboard and is settled only by observation.
precedents.reason: law.md: internal sensors read life signs and can be tuned to look for something specific; the lore agent's reading of TNG 101 found a collision alert sounding automatically at the barrier. Alert condition is the captain's.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] La Forge beamed back from the Farpoint tunnels with Yar and Troi and was on the bridge, at the aft stations, for both of Q's in-person appearances near Deneb IV; Worf had the helm. He was not aboard at the barrier.
precedents.reason: Canon shows him beamed back before the first appearance and on the bridge at the end, and is silent on where he stood in between; a conn officer returning to the bridge in a crisis is the plausible reading. Checked by a fresh agent against the TNG 101 transcript.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] The bridge's environmental sensors map temperature across the room only coarsely, and its optical pickups work in the visible and near infrared. Thermal imaging fine enough to tell a face from a collar needs dedicated long-wave infrared pickups; physics asks little of them (about a centimetre of aperture resolves a centimetre at ten metres at body-heat wavelengths), so fitting them is a small engineering job, a few hours for engineering's people.
precedents.reason: M-010: the near channel is real imaging, bound by diffraction and wavelength. Body heat peaks near 9.3 micrometres (Wien), which ordinary visible-band pickups don't image. CALC at L:1:11.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] The captain has a yeoman, a crewman on the bridge support staff, who keeps his appointments and routes requests for his time.
precedents.reason: Canon shows yeomen as a Starfleet billet (TOS) and is silent on Picard's appointments; the most plausible reading of how a flagship captain's time is booked.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] Hesker IV's colony transmitter is too weak for a live call at the Enterprise's present range; messages each way take about forty minutes now and grow quicker as the ship closes.
precedents.reason: M-013: FTL signalling speed rises with transmitter power and relays; a lone ship's floor (~52,000 c, CALC) gives about 41 minutes for 4.1 ly; a small colony's transmitter adds nothing to that.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] A cargo bay can be isolated on its own environmental circuit and run at negative pressure with filtered exhaust, making a contained ward; doing it takes engineering a shift or so and competes with other replicator and power work.
precedents.reason: Cargo bays have their own environmental controls; negative-pressure isolation is ordinary hospital engineering; canon uses cargo bays for overflow and refugees.

precedents.ruling: The VISOR keeps no record; its signal runs live to La Forge's implants. A tap on the VISOR can carry its output to the ship to be displayed and recorded, but building one is a project: the signal is hard to encode and unstable, and the raw image means little to anyone but La Forge without his reading of it. In this branch La Forge and Data begin it at 41175.4, prompted by the first officer.
precedents.reason: Card K-050: canon's visual acuity transmitter, a La Forge and Data project of 2364, in field use by 41503.7; canon doesn't say when it was begun.

precedents.ruling: Who may be on the bridge, civilians included, is the captain's decision; the first officer can arrange a visit only with his agreement.
precedents.reason: voices.md: Wesley's bridge access is the captain's decision; canon season one shows Picard deciding it himself.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] The nearest starbase with a drydock able to take a Galaxy-class ship is Starbase 49, 16.0 light years from Hesker IV. Standard cruise is warp 6.
precedents.reason: Canon places Farpoint at the frontier beyond Deneb and gives no starbase nearby; a frontier region would have few large drydocks. Warp 6 as standard cruise follows the TNG writers' convention.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] Emergency stores (power cells, medical and survival supplies held against disaster) are released only on a senior command code: the captain's or the first officer's.
precedents.reason: Emergency reserves exist so they are there in an emergency; releasing them is a command decision with a record (deeds.md authorisation trace).

precedents.ruling: [assumed] Hesker IV's local day runs nearly in step with ship's time at this season; colony times quoted in messages are close enough to ship's time to read as such.
precedents.reason: A convenience for reading colony messages; nothing in the episode depends on the offset.

precedents.ruling: [assumed] The first officer's quarters have a small galley, a cooktop and a compact oven, enough to cook and bake by hand from replicated raw ingredients.
precedents.reason: Canon shows Riker cooking in his own quarters (Time Squared, 2365); Lloyd lived Riker's life and keeps the habit (sheet).
